title: The Lighthouse Keeper
text:
Margaret had kept the lighthouse for thirty years, and she knew every rock along the coast. One stormy evening, a small boat appeared near the cliffs with no lights. She grabbed her lantern and climbed the narrow stairs as quickly as she could.

Below, a young fisherman was shouting for help, his boat already tilting in the waves. Margaret signalled to him with the lamp, guiding him toward the safe channel. Within minutes, he reached the harbour, shaking but alive. He later said that he had never seen a light so steady in his life.

questions.text: How long had Margaret kept the lighthouse?
What did Margaret use to guide the fisherman?
Why was the boat's lack of lights especially dangerous?
options: It made the boat easier to steer
Nobody on shore could easily see where the boat was
It showed the fisherman was lost on purpose
It meant the boat had already sunk

questions.text: What does the fisherman's remark suggest about Margaret?
options: She was careless with her lamp
She was calm and skilled under pressure
She was afraid of the sea
She wanted to leave the lighthouse

vocabulary.definition: a light inside a protective case that can be carried
tall, steep rock faces, usually beside the sea
not shaking or moving; staying the same
a narrow stretch of water that boats can safely travel through

paragraph_translations: Margaret cuidava do farol há trinta anos, e conhecia cada rochedo da costa. Numa noite de tempestade, um pequeno barco apareceu perto das falésias, sem luzes. Ela pegou sua lanterna e subiu as escadas estreitas o mais rápido que pôde.

Lá embaixo, um jovem pescador gritava por socorro, com o barco já inclinado sobre as ondas. Margaret sinalizou para ele com a lamparina, guiando-o em direção ao canal seguro. Em poucos minutos, ele chegou ao porto, tremendo, mas vivo. Mais tarde, ele disse que nunca tinha visto uma luz tão firme na vida.
